语言主要是一种交流工具，而非思维工具

Language is primarily a tool for communication rather than thought

Evelina Fedorenko1,2、Steven T. Piantadosi3 与 Edward A. F. Gibson1

Evelina Fedorenko1,2, Steven T. Piantadosi3 & Edward A. F. Gibson1

Nature 第 630 卷，2024 年 6 月 20 日，575–586 页（观点文章）。https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-024-07522-w。收稿：2023 年 2 月 15 日；接受：2024 年 5 月 3 日；在线发表：2024 年 6 月 19 日。

Nature Vol 630, 20 June 2024, 575–586 (Perspective). https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-024-07522-w. Received: 15 February 2023; Accepted: 3 May 2024; Published online: 19 June 2024.

1美国马萨诸塞州剑桥，麻省理工学院。2美国马萨诸塞州波士顿，哈佛大学言语与听觉生物科学与技术项目。3美国加利福尼亚州伯克利，加州大学伯克利分校。电子邮件：evelina9@mit.edu

1Massachusetts Institute of Technology, Cambridge, MA, USA. 2Speech and Hearing in Bioscience and Technology Program at Harvard University, Boston, MA, USA. 3University of California, Berkeley, Berkeley, CA, USA. e-mail: evelina9@mit.edu

语言是我们这一物种的决定性特征，但它所服务的功能（一种或多种）已争论了数个世纪。本文我们援引来自神经科学及相关学科的最新证据，论证在现代人类中，语言是一种交流工具，这与“我们用语言来思考”这一颇具影响的观点相反。我们首先介绍支持人类语言能力的脑网络；随后回顾语言与思维之间存在双重分离的证据，并讨论语言的若干特性，这些特性表明语言是为交流而优化的。我们的结论是：尽管语言的出现无疑改变了人类文化，但语言似乎并不是复杂思维（包括符号思维）的先决条件。相反，语言是传递文化知识的强大工具；它很可能与我们的思维和推理能力协同演化，并且只是反映了、而非造就了人类认知标志性的复杂精妙。

Language is a defining characteristic of our species, but the function, or functions, that it serves has been debated for centuries. Here we bring recent evidence from neuroscience and allied disciplines to argue that in modern humans, language is a tool for communication, contrary to a prominent view that we use language for thinking. We begin by introducing the brain network that supports linguistic ability in humans. We then review evidence for a double dissociation between language and thought, and discuss several properties of language that suggest that it is optimized for communication. We conclude that although the emergence of language has unquestionably transformed human culture, language does not appear to be a prerequisite for complex thought, including symbolic thought. Instead, language is a powerful tool for the transmission of cultural knowledge; it plausibly co-evolved with our thinking and reasoning capacities, and only reflects, rather than gives rise to, the signature sophistication of human cognition.

据估计，语言在人类中出现于距今 10 万至 100 万年之间1。语言的功能及其起源的因果驱动因素，长期以来在哲学、语言学、认知科学、进化生物学和人类学等众多领域中争论激烈。主导这一讨论的有两大类假说，尽管二者并不相互排斥。一种观点认为，语言主要服务于交流功能——它使我们能够彼此分享知识、想法和感受2–7。另一种观点认为，语言介导思维和认知8–13。关于语言在思维中作用的具体假说，从强主张（语言是所有形式的思维——至少是命题性思维——所必需的14,15），到较弱的主张（语言可能只对思维与推理的某些方面至关重要，或能促进这些方面9,16），再到认为语言在发展过程中帮助搭建某些类型学习的“脚手架”、但在成熟大脑中可能不再需要的主张12,17,18（专栏 1），不一而足。

Language is estimated to have emerged in humans between 100,000 and 1,000,000 years ago1. The functions of language and the causal drivers in its origins have long been fiercely debated across diverse fields, including philosophy, linguistics, cognitive science, evolutionary biology and anthropology. Two broad hypotheses have dominated this discussion, although they are not mutually exclusive. One proposal is that language primarily serves a communicative function—it enables us to share knowledge, thoughts, and feelings with one another2–7. Another proposal is that language mediates thinking and cognition8–13. The specific hypotheses about the role of language in thinking have ranged from strong claims that language is necessary for all forms of (at least propositional) thought14,15, to weaker claims that language may only be critical for, or can facilitate, certain aspects of thinking and reasoning9,16, and claims that language helps scaffold certain kinds of learning during development but may no longer be needed in mature brains12,17,18 (Box 1).

从进化适应度的角度看，语言的交流功能和认知功能都可能带来适应性优势。准确传递信息的能力很可能有助于狩猎、拾荒和长途迁徙等合作行为，并使知识和技能得以传给后代（文化传递）。推理能力的提升则很可能带来更复杂的计划与决策、更好的工具制造以及更强的问题解决能力。然而，关于认知特征进化起源的假说是出了名的难以评估19。关于早期人族生活的主要证据来自稀少的考古记录。大脑不会形成化石；即便能形成化石，从大脑的大小、形状和解剖结构中也只能获得关于脑功能的粗略信息。此外，某些特征可能因某一原因而进化，随后却因物种生态的变化而服务于不同的功能：这种现象被称为扩展适应（exaptation）20。鉴于这些挑战，我们并不打算对语言的进化起源做出强有力的论断。不过，我们确实就语言在现代人类中的功能提出论证，并讨论塑造了语言的优化压力。

From an evolutionary fitness standpoint, both the communicative and the cognitive functions of language could provide adaptive advantages. An ability to accurately transmit information would plausibly facilitate cooperative behaviours such as hunting, scavenging and long-distance travel, and enable passing of knowledge and skills to offspring (cultural transmission). An improved reasoning capacity would plausibly enable more sophisticated planning and decision making, creation of better tools and better problem-solving abilities. However, hypotheses about the evolutionary origins of cognitive traits are notoriously challenging to evaluate19. The primary evidence about the lives of early hominins comes from sparse archaeological records. Brains do not fossilize, and even if they did, only coarse information about brain function could be gleaned from brain size, shape and anatomy. Moreover, certain traits may evolve for one reason but subsequently serve a different function owing to changes in the species’ ecology: a phenomenon known as exaptation20. As a result of these challenges, we do not aspire to make strong claims about the evolutionary origins of language. We do, however, make an argument about the function of language in modern humans and discuss optimization pressures that have shaped language.

“语言用于思维”与“语言用于交流”这两种主张，至少其中某些变体对人类的认知与神经架构以及人类语言的特性做出了可检验的预测。是否有任何形式的思维——我们关于世界的知识以及基于这些知识表征进行推理的能力——需要语言（即支持我们生成和理解具有意义结构的词序列的表征与计算）？如果某些形式的思维需要语言，那么至少在这些类型的思维与推理中，语言机制应当被必然地调用，而且没有语言，这些类型的思维就不可能发生。如果语言是一种交流工具，那么语言应当显示出高效信息传递的标志性特征。直到最近，这些预测都难以评估。然而，在过去二十年间，已出现了能够为语言功能提供关键启示的知识和工具。首先，在破解语言的神经架构方面取得了重大进展，为评估各种形式的思维过程中语言加工机制是否被调用提供了明确的“靶标”。其次，大量多样语言的语料库已广泛可得，同时出现了一套强大的计算工具（通常基于信息论21），可用于严格刻画语言系统。因此，现在正是盘点关于语言功能及其在人类认知中作用这些重大问题之现有证据的时机。

At least some variants of both the language-for-thought and the language-for-communication proposals make testable predictions about human cognitive and neural architecture and about the properties of human languages. Do any forms of thought—our knowledge of the world and ability to reason over these knowledge representations—require language (that is, representations and computations that support our ability to generate and interpret meaningfully structured word sequences)? If some forms of thought require language, then linguistic mechanisms should be obligatorily engaged for at least those types of thinking and reasoning, and those types of thought should not be possible without language. If language is a tool for communication, then language should show hallmarks of efficient information transfer. Until recently, these predictions have been difficult to evaluate. However, over the past two decades, knowledge and tools have become available that have shed critical light on the function of language. First, substantial advances have been made in deciphering the neural architecture of language, providing a clear ‘target’ for evaluating the engagement of language-processing mechanisms during various forms of thought. Second, massive corpora of diverse languages have become widely available, along with a suite of powerful computational tools, often based on information theory21, for rigorously characterizing linguistic systems. As a result, the time is now ripe to take stock of current evidence on the big and important questions of the function of language and its role in human cognition.

人脑中的语言网络

The language network in the human brain

我们的语言知识涵盖语言结构各个层面（从语音到句子）的规律性知识，以及大量的形式–意义映射22,23（语素、词和构式的意义）。借助这些知识，我们既能向他人传达自己的想法，也能从他人的话语中推断其意图表达的意义。语言产出和语言理解由左半球一组相互连接的脑区支持，这组脑区常被称为“语言网络”24–27（近期综述见参考文献 28）（图 1a；专栏 2 描述了它与语言神经生物学“经典模型”的关系）。

Our knowledge of language encompasses knowledge of regularities at all levels of linguistic structure, from sounds to sentences, and a large set of form–meaning mappings22,23 (meanings of morphemes, words and constructions). Using this knowledge, we can both convey our thoughts to others and infer others’ intended meanings from their utterances. Language production and language understanding are supported by an interconnected set of brain areas in the left hemisphere, often referred to as the ‘language network’24–27 (recently reviewed in ref. 28) (Fig. 1a; Box 2 describes its relationship to the ‘classic model’ of the neurobiology of language).

语言网络的两个特性对于讨论语言的功能至关重要。第一，语言脑区表现出对输入和输出模态的独立性——这是表征抽象性的关键标志。首先，在理解过程中，这些脑区对各种模态（口语、书面语或手语29–32）的语言输入均有反应。同样，在语言生成过程中，无论我们是通过说还是写来产出信息，这些脑区都会激活33。这些脑区同时支持理解和产出33,34（图 1a），这表明它们很可能储存着我们的语言知识，而编码和解码语言信息都需要这些知识。语言网络表征的抽象性表明，该网络对应于 Hauser、Chomsky 和 Fitch 在一篇关于语言进化的有影响力的文章35中所称的“狭义语言官能”，即一个独立于较低层级的言语感知和言语发音机制的“抽象计算系统”（专栏 2）。

Two properties of the language network are important for the discussion of the function(s) of language. First, the language areas exhibit independence of input and output modalities—key signatures of representational abstractness. First, during comprehension, these brain areas respond to linguistic input across modalities (spoken, written or signed29–32). Similarly, during language generation, these areas are active regardless of whether we produce our messages by speaking or writing33. The fact that these areas support both comprehension and production33,34 (Fig. 1a) suggests that they are likely to store our linguistic knowledge, which is needed to both encode and decode linguistic messages. The abstractness of the language network’s representations suggests that this network corresponds to what Hauser, Chomsky and Fitch, in an influential piece on language evolution35, referred to as “the faculty of language in the narrow sense” or an “abstract computational system” that is separate from lower-level speech perception and speech articulation mechanisms (Box 2).

第二，语言脑区既表征和加工词义，也表征和加工句法结构——这是对“语言用于思维”诸假说至关重要的两个语言成分（专栏 1）。具体而言，来自功能磁共振成像（fMRI）、脑磁图和颅内记录研究中多种实验范式与自然范式的证据表明，语言网络的所有脑区都对词义以及词与词之间的句法和语义依存关系敏感33,36–48（图 1a）。综上，语言网络中语言表征的抽象性及其对语言意义和结构的敏感性，使它成为评估关于语言在思维与认知中作用的各种假说的明确靶标（专栏 3）。

Second, the language areas represent and process both word meanings and syntactic structure—two components of language that are important to the language-for-thought hypotheses (Box 1). In particular, evidence from diverse experimental and naturalistic paradigms in functional MRI (fMRI), magnetoencephalography and intracranial recording studies has revealed that all areas of the language network are sensitive to word meanings and to inter-word syntactic and semantic dependencies33,36–48 (Fig. 1a). Together, the abstractness of the linguistic representations in the language network and the sensitivity of the network to linguistic meaning and structure make it a clear target for evaluating hypotheses about the role of language in thought and cognition (Box 3).

语言对于思维既不必要也不充分

Language is not necessary or sufficient for thought

人类认知的本体论以及介导思维的心理表征的本质（专栏 3）仍是活跃的研究领域。宽泛地说，思维包括我们关于世界的知识（包括特定领域的知识，如关于物体物理属性的知识或关于社会主体的知识），以及基于这些知识表征进行的推理，其中包括做出推断和预测。除了针对特定知识领域的推理之外，推理还可能涉及跨领域的信息整合（这是类比推理的重要成分49），或者是领域一般性的、脱离任何特定领域的推理。领域一般性推理常与流体智力的概念相联系50。由于各种“语言用于思维”假说在语言被认为对思维或认知的哪些方面至关重要或有帮助这一点上各不相同（专栏 1），而我们的目标是对这一观点做广泛评估，因此我们将讨论来自多种调用思维与推理的范式的证据。此外，从经验上看，迄今测试过的思维的所有方面在调用语言资源方面表现相似。

The ontology of human cognition and the nature of mental representations that mediate thought (Box 3) remain active areas of research. Broadly, thought encompasses our knowledge of the world (including particular domains, such as knowledge of the physical properties of objects or knowledge of social agents) and reasoning over these knowledge representations, which includes making inferences and predictions. Aside from reasoning about particular knowledge domains, reasoning can involve cross-domain integration of information (an important ingredient of analogical reasoning49) or be domain-general, abstracted away from any particular domain. Domain-general reasoning is often linked to the notion of fluid intelligence50. Because language-for-thought hypotheses vary in what aspects of thought or cognition language is supposed to be critical or helpful for (Box 1) and our goal is to evaluate this idea broadly, we discuss evidence from diverse paradigms that engage thinking and reasoning. Moreover, empirically, all aspects of thought tested so far behave similarly with respect to their recruitment of linguistic resources.

专栏 1 “语言用于思维”假说的多种版本

Box 1 Many flavours of the language-for-thought hypothesis

全面回顾以往关于语言在思维中作用的主张超出了本文的范围（相关综述见例如参考文献 9,10,12,16,71,178–182）。不过，我们要强调这一问题上观点的多样性以及理论格局的复杂性。关于语言在思维中作用的主张至少在四个维度上有所不同（样例引文以及“我们用语言思考”这一观点为何吸引许多人的原因见补充信息）。第一，各主张在语言对思维影响的范围上不同：从主张所有思维（至少所有命题性思维）都需要语言表征，到主张只有某些类型的思维需要。第二个维度涉及语言对思维的重要程度：从主张语言表征是思维所必需的（即无法获取这些表征就不可能思考），到主张它们只是增强或促进思维（即使某些目标思维任务的表现更快和/或更准确）。第三个维度与所涉及的语言表征的性质有关。有些主张强调所有自然语言共有的特征，包括词语和句法结构；另一些主张则关注特定语言所特有的特征——例如，某种语言是否有表示某一特定概念的词，或是否标记某一特定语法区别（补充信息）。最后，各主张在语言对思维产生影响的时间上不同：有些主张认为语言表征对思维能力的发展是必需的或有帮助的，另一些则认为即使在完全成熟的大脑中，语言表征对思维仍然重要。

A comprehensive review of prior claims about the role of language in thinking is outside the scope of this Perspective (for reviews, see for example refs. 9,10,12,16,71,178–182). However, we emphasize the diversity of perspectives on this issue and the complexity of the theoretical landscape. Proposals about the role of language in thinking vary along at least four dimensions (sample quotes and reasons why the idea that we use language to think appeals to many are presented in the Supplementary Information). First, proposals vary in the scope of the effects of language on thought: from claims that all of thought (at least all propositional thought) requires linguistic representations to claims that only certain kinds of thinking do. The second dimension concerns the degree of importance of language for thought, from claims that linguistic representations are necessary for thinking (such that without access to these representations, thinking is not possible) to claims that they only augment or facilitate thinking (that is, enable faster and/or more accurate performance on some target thinking task). The third dimension has to do with the nature of linguistic representations that are at play. Some proposals emphasize features that are common to all natural languages, including words and syntactic structure. Other proposals instead focus on features that are specific to particular languages—for instance, whether a language has a word for a particular concept or marks a particular grammatical distinction (Supplementary Information). Finally, proposals vary as to the timing of the effects of language on thought, with some proposals arguing that linguistic representations are necessary or helpful for the development of thinking abilities, and others arguing that linguistic representations continue to be important for thinking even in fully mature brains.

较强的主张，例如认为所有形式的思维都需要语言表征的理论，当然最容易被证伪。对于认为只有某些类型的思维需要语言表征的理论，关键在于清楚界定相关思维类型的范围——理想情况下还应提出调用这些思维形式的具体范式——从而使假说可被经验检验。在已明确提出具体主张的情况下（例如参考文献 9,72,74），这些主张并未在神经科学研究中得到支持，而且某些行为效应也不能明确归因于语言网络（例如参考文献 70）。事实上，正如本文所讨论的，至少就成熟大脑而言，目前没有明确的经验证据支持任何形式的思维需要语言表征（词语或句法结构）。同样，对于认为语言表征促进思维的理论，关键在于描述应在何种条件下观察到此类效应，并说明其性质以及——理想情况下——推定的神经机制。目前关于语言对思维可能的促进效应以及语言在某些认知能力发展中可能作用的证据复杂且有争议（详见补充信息）。似乎很清楚的是，我们可以用语言把模拟信号压缩为符号表征（例如把由九个物体组成的视觉阵列简化为“九”183；关于信息压缩在人类思维中作用的近期主张见参考文献 173）。然而，这些表征不一定是专门的语言表征：它们可以是符号性的但非语言的（例如“9”），而使用非语言符号表征并不调用语言资源（例如，数学推理在语言脑区不引起任何反应，并且在严重失语症患者中得以保留51,77–79）。

Stronger claims, such as accounts whereby all forms of thought require linguistic representations, are of course the easiest to falsify. For accounts whereby only certain kinds of thought require linguistic representations, it is critical to clearly define the scope of the relevant kinds of thought—and ideally, to suggest particular paradigms that engage those forms of thinking—to render the hypotheses empirically testable. In cases where specific proposals have been articulated (for example, in refs. 9,72,74), they have not found empirical support in neuroscientific investigations, and some of the behavioural effects cannot be unambiguously attributed to the language network (for example, ref. 70). Indeed, as discussed in this Perspective, at least for mature brains, there is at present no unequivocal empirical support for any form of thinking requiring linguistic representations (words or syntactic structures). Similarly, for accounts whereby linguistic representations facilitate thinking, it is critical to delineate the conditions under which such effects should be observed and to describe their nature and—ideally—putative neural mechanisms. Current bodies of evidence for potential facilitative effects of language on thinking and potential roles of language in the development of certain cognitive capacities are complex and controversial (further details in Supplementary Information). It seems clear that we can use language to compress analogue signals into symbolic representations (for example, reducing a visual array of nine objects to ‘nine’183; see ref. 173 for a recent proposal on the role of information compression in human thinking). However, these representations need not be specifically linguistic: they could be symbolic but non-linguistic (for example, ‘9’), and the use of symbolic non-linguistic representations does not engage linguistic resources (for example, mathematical reasoning elicits no response in the language brain areas and is preserved in individuals with severe aphasia51,77–79).

如果语言介导了某些形式的思维，那么在没有语言的情况下，这些形式的思维就不应可能发生，因为它们应关键地依赖于语言表征（“语言对思维的必要性”论证）。此外，语言的存在（或完好的语言能力）应当与进行这些形式思维的能力相关联（“语言对思维的充分性”论证）。我们依次讨论这两点。

If language mediates some forms of thought, then those forms of thought should not be possible in the absence of language because they should critically depend on linguistic representations (the ‘necessity of language for thought’ argument). Moreover, the presence of language (or an intact linguistic ability) should be associated with the capacity for those forms of thought (the ‘sufficiency of language for thought’ argument). We discuss these points in turn.

语言对于任何已测试的思维形式都不是必需的

Language is not necessary for any tested forms of thought

推断脑–行为关联与分离的经典方法是考察脑损伤或脑疾病患者。如果语言能力介导我们进行某些形式思维的能力，那么语言障碍就应伴随这些方面思维与推理的困难。证据是明确无疑的——有许多个体存在严重的语言障碍（同时影响词汇和句法能力），却仍表现出从事多种形式思维的完好能力——他们能解决数学问题51,52，执行计划并遵循非言语指令53，从事多种形式的推理，包括形式逻辑推理、关于世界的因果推理和科学推理54–58，理解他人的信念或想法并进行语用推断53,56,59–62，在世界中导航63，以及对物体和事件做出语义判断64–70（图 1b）。

The classical approach for making inferences about brain–behaviour associations and dissociations is to examine individuals with brain damage or disorders. If linguistic ability mediates our ability to engage in certain forms of thought, then linguistic impairments should be associated with concomitant difficulties in those aspects of thinking and reasoning. The evidence is unequivocal—there are many cases of individuals with severe linguistic impairments, affecting both lexical and syntactic abilities, who nevertheless exhibit intact abilities to engage in many forms of thought—they can solve mathematical problems51,52, perform executive planning and follow non-verbal instructions53, engage in diverse forms of reasoning, including formal logical reasoning, causal reasoning about the world and scientific reasoning54–58, to understand what another person believes or thinks and perform pragmatic inference53,56,59–62, to navigate in the world63, and to make semantic judgements about objects and events64–70 (Fig. 1b).

专栏 2 从语言神经生物学的经典模型到当前认识

Box 2 From the classic model of the neurobiology of language to where we are now

许多教科书仍在使用语言神经基础的经典模型，该模型由 Wernicke 提出184，并经 Lichtheim 和 Geschwind 加以阐发和修订24,185。该模型由两个皮层区域组成——额下回皮层中的布洛卡区和颞上回后部皮层中的韦尼克区——它们被认为分别支持语言产出和语言理解，并由一条背侧纤维束（弓状束）相连（图 a）。多年来该模型受到不少批评27,186,187——但尽管不完整，经典模型正确地捕捉到了语言神经生物学的关键方面。我们认为，关于布洛卡区和韦尼克区的许多混淆，源于在实验设计和科学话语中频繁混淆言语（口语的形式）与语言（形式到意义映射的抽象系统），以及人类认知神经科学主要依赖脑区的解剖学定义而非功能定义。

Many textbooks continue to use the classic model of the neural basis of language, which was proposed by Wernicke184 and elaborated and revised by Lichteim and Geschwind24,185. This model consists of two cortical areas—Broca’s area in the inferior frontal cortex and Wernicke’s area in the posterior superior temporal cortex—which are argued to support language production and comprehension, respectively, and which are connected by a dorsal fibre bundle (the arcuate fasciculus) (panel a). This model has received criticism over the years27,186,187—but, although incomplete, the classic model correctly captures key aspects of the neurobiology of language. We believe that much of the confusion about Broca’s and Wernicke’s areas has resulted from frequent conflation of speech (the form of spoken language) and language (the abstract system of form-to-meaning mappings) in experimental designs and scientific discourse, and predominant reliance in human cognitive neuroscience on anatomical rather than functional definitions of brain areas.

正如原始文献所述，布洛卡和韦尼克发现的脑区分别支持言语运动（发音）计划和言语感知。当前的神经科学证据有力支持在额下回皮层中存在一个发音选择性脑区188–192（图 b，红色），以及在颞上回中存在一个言语感知选择性脑区193–197（图 b，蓝色）。与语言网络脑区不同，这些脑区对语言意义不敏感，只对语言信号的表层属性敏感28。在这些脑区的名称中加入功能（例如“布洛卡发音计划区”和“韦尼克言语感知区”），并使用经过验证的“定位”范式将这些脑区与邻近的功能上不同的脑区区分开，很可能会推动进展并减少混淆28。

As described in the original sources, the brain areas that were discovered by Broca and Wernicke support speech motor (articulatory) planning and speech perception, respectively. Current neuroscientific evidence strongly supports the existence of an articulation-selective area in the inferior frontal cortex188–192 (panel b, red) and of an area selective for speech perception in the superior temporal gyrus193–197 (panel b, blue). In contrast to the language network areas, these areas are not sensitive to linguistic meaning, only to the surface properties of linguistic signals28. Adding function into these areas’ names (for example, ‘Broca’s articulatory planning area’ and ‘Wernicke’s speech perception area’) and using validated ‘localizer’ paradigms to separate these areas from nearby functionally distinct areas is likely to lead to progress and alleviate confusion28.

经典模型中缺少的是“高级语言脑区”，它们储存抽象的语言知识并支持理解和产出，如“人脑中的语言网络”一节所述（图 1a 及图 b，紫色）。对于早期语言神经生物学理论中缺少这些脑区，有一个直接的解释。关于脑–行为关系的早期证据来自脑损伤后选择性缺陷的报告。由于布洛卡区和韦尼克区相对局限且专门负责特定功能，它们受损更可能导致缺陷（因为没有其他脑区支持这些功能）。相比之下，高级语言网络分布在左侧颞叶和额叶皮层的广泛区域（图 1a 及图 b，紫色），不同语言区域表现出相似的功能特征28（其他观点见参考文献 27,198,199）。因此，与言语发音区和言语感知区不同，高级语言网络中可能没有哪个单独部分是语言功能所关键必需的。事实上，语言网络的局限性病灶并不会导致严重或持久的缺陷，尽管与言语感知区相邻的颞叶后部成分可能相对更为重要200。

Absent from the classic model are the ‘higher-level language areas’, which store abstract linguistic knowledge and support comprehension and production, as discussed in ‘The language network in the human brain’ (Fig. 1a and panel b, purple). There is a straightforward explanation for the absence of these areas from the early proposals of the neurobiology of language. The early evidence about brain–behaviour relationships came from reports of selective deficits following brain damage. Because Broca’s and Wernicke’s areas are relatively circumscribed and specialized for particular functions, their damage is more likely to lead to deficits (given that no other brain areas support these functions). By contrast, the higher-level language network is distributed across extensive portions of the left temporal and frontal cortex (Fig. 1a and panel b, purple), with different language regions exhibiting similar functional profiles28 (alternative proposals are described in refs. 27,198,199). As a result, in contrast to speech articulation and speech perception areas, no individual part of the high-level language network may be critically needed for linguistic function. Indeed, circumscribed lesions to the language network do not lead to severe or long-lasting deficits, although the posterior temporal component, which is adjacent to the speech perception area, may be relatively more important200.

经典模型与当前模型。| a，语言神经生物学的经典模型。b，基于当前语言神经生物学知识的模型（其他观点见参考文献 27,198,199）。这一更新后的模型仍包括布洛卡（发音计划）区188–192和韦尼克（言语感知）区193–197，但另外还包括一组共同支持高级语言理解和产出的额叶和颞叶区域28（另见图 1a）。作为背景，我们还显示了初级听觉皮层（它很可能为韦尼克言语感知区提供输入）和感觉运动皮层（布洛卡发音计划区很可能向其提供输入）189,190。图中标注：布洛卡区（语言产出）；韦尼克区（语言理解）；布洛卡发音计划区（在言语产出中计划口面部运动）；感觉运动皮层（控制口面部运动，包括但不限于言语发音时）；初级听觉皮层（声音感知，包括但不限于言语感知时）；语言网络（非模态的语言理解与产出）；韦尼克言语感知区（在言语感知中加工语音）。

Classic and current models. | a, The classic model of the neurobiology of language. b, A model based on the current knowledge of neurobiology of language (alternative proposals are described in refs. 27,198,199). This updated model still includes Broca’s (articulatory planning) area188–192 and Wernicke’s (speech perception) area193–197, but additionally includes a set of frontal and temporal areas that jointly support high-level language comprehension and production28 (also see Fig. 1a). For context, we also show primary auditory cortex, which is likely to provide input to Wernicke’s (speech perception) area, and sensorimotor cortex, to which Broca’s (articulatory planning) area is likely to provide input189,190. Figure labels: Broca’s area (language production); Wernicke’s area (language comprehension); Broca’s articulatory planning area (planning oro-facial movements during speech production); Sensorimotor cortex (control of oro-facial movements, including—but not selectively—during speech articulation); Primary auditory cortex (sound perception, including—but not selectively—during speech perception); Language network (amodal language comprehension and production); Wernicke’s speech perception area (processing speech sounds during speech perception).

重要的是，在这些研究中，研究者仔细而系统地评估了个体的语言能力，以确保缺陷涉及的是语言能力（包括词汇和句法加工），而非较低层级的感知或运动能力71。这一系列证据既挑战了关于语言对思维重要性的一般性主张（专栏 1），也挑战了若干关于语言在特定类型思维中起关键作用的具体主张，包括数学推理72、跨领域信息整合9,73和分类74。尽管丧失了语言能力，一些严重失语症患者仍能完成所有已测试形式的思维与推理，这体现在他们在多种认知任务上的完好表现。他们只是无法将这些想法映射到语言表达上——无论是在语言产出中（无法通过语言向他人传达想法），还是在理解中（无法从他人的词句中提取意义）（图 1b）。当然，在某些脑损伤病例中，语言能力和（部分）思维能力可能同时受影响，但考虑到语言系统与其他高级认知系统在位置上的邻近75,76，这是可以预料的。

Importantly, in these studies, researchers carefully and systematically assessed the individuals’ linguistic abilities to ensure that the deficit concerns linguistic ability, including lexical and syntactic processing, and not the lower-level perceptual or motor abilities71. This body of evidence challenges both general claims about the importance of language for thought (Box 1), and a number of specific proposals about the critical role of language in particular kinds of thinking, including mathematical reasoning72, cross-domain information integration9,73 and categorization74. Despite losing their linguistic ability, some individuals with severe aphasia are able to perform all tested forms of thinking and reasoning, as evidenced by their intact performance on diverse cognitive tasks. They simply cannot map those thoughts onto linguistic expressions, either in language production (they cannot convey their thoughts to others through language) or in understanding (they cannot extract meaning from others’ words and sentences) (Fig. 1b). Of course, in some cases of brain damage, both linguistic and (some) thinking abilities may be affected, but this is to be expected given the proximity of the language system to other high-level cognitive systems75,76.

神经影像学证据补充了来自脑损伤个体的证据。借助 fMRI 等工具，我们可以在完好、健康的大脑中识别语言脑区，然后在个体从事需要不同形式思维的任务时考察这些脑区的反应。在“人脑中的语言网络”一节中，我们为评估此类假说定义了一个明确的靶标：语言网络，即在我们理解和产出语言时普遍被调用的一组脑区28（图 1a）。研究者已考察了该网络对多种非语言输入和任务的反应，证据表明，在所有已测试的思维形式中，语言网络的所有区域基本都处于“沉默”状态，包括数学推理77–79、形式逻辑推理80,81、执行高要求的执行功能任务（如工作记忆或认知控制任务）77、理解计算机代码82,83、思考他人的心理状态84–86，以及对物体或事件做出语义判断69,70,87。相反，这些任务调用的是与语言网络不重叠的其他脑区（图 1b），尽管它们有时紧邻语言脑区75,76。未来的研究仍有可能发现某些会调用语言脑区、且对失语症患者构成挑战的思维任务，但迄今尚未发现此类任务。

Neuroimaging evidence complements the evidence from individuals with brain damage. Using tools such as fMRI, we can identify the language areas in intact, healthy brains and then examine the response in those areas while individuals engage in tasks that require different forms of thought. In ‘The language network in the human brain’, we defined a clear target for evaluating such hypotheses: the language network, a set of brain areas that are ubiquitously engaged when we understand and produce language28 (Fig. 1a). Responses in this network to diverse non-linguistic inputs and tasks have been examined, and the evidence demonstrates that all regions of the language network are largely ‘silent’ during all tested forms of thought, including mathematical reasoning77–79, formal logical reasoning80,81, performing demanding executive function tasks such as working memory or cognitive control tasks77, understanding computer code82,83, thinking about others’ mental states84–86, and making semantic judgments about objects or events69,70,87. Instead, these tasks engage other brain areas that are non-overlapping with the language network (Fig. 1b), although they sometimes lie in close proximity to the language areas75,76. It remains possible that future work will uncover some thinking tasks that will engage language areas and that will prove challenging for patients with aphasia, but no such tasks have been found so far.

有些“语言用于思维”假说专门涉及认知发展（专栏 1）。根据这些假说，语言（或在某些理论中，更一般的符号表征）可能对某些类型或方式的思维的发展至关重要12,17,18,88,89。对这一观点的某些支持来自如下研究：教儿童或非人灵长类表示某些概念（例如“相同”这一概念）的词或符号，或以突出世界中与任务相关维度的方式分配标签（例如把较大的物体标为“爸爸”、较小的标为“宝宝”，以引起对物体大小的注意），可以使其在某些关系推理任务上获得成功18。另有研究者认为，训练幼儿掌握某些句法构式（例如补语从句）可使他们通过心理理论任务17,90,91。然而，存在怀疑的理由。第一，最近的证据表明，语言网络与支持思维和推理的系统之间的分离在幼儿身上就已存在92,93（专栏 3），这与“在早期发展阶段思维依赖语言资源”的可能性相矛盾。第二，一些在无法接触语言的环境中成长的儿童仍能进行复杂的推理。特别是，一些父母听力正常的聋童在成长过程中很少或根本接触不到语言，有时长达数年，因为他们听不到言语，而父母或照料者又不懂手语。缺乏语言接触会对认知的许多方面造成有害后果94,95，鉴于语言是了解世界的关键信息来源96,97，这是可以预料的。尽管如此，经历过语言剥夺的个体无疑表现出复杂认知功能的能力：他们仍能学习数学、进行关系推理、建立因果链，并获得丰富而精深的世界知识98,99（另见参考文献 100，其中提供了来自一例虐童案中语言剥夺的更具争议性的证据）。换言之，无法接触语言表征并不会使从事复杂的（包括符号性的）思维从根本上变得不可能，尽管推理的某些方面确实表现出延迟101,102。由此看来，在典型发展中，语言和推理是平行发展的（来自脑进化的一致证据见“人类与动物中的交流与思维”一节）。

Some language-for-thought hypotheses specifically concern cognitive development (Box 1). According to these hypotheses, language (or, in some accounts, symbolic representations more generally) may be critical for the development of certain kinds or ways of thinking12,17,18,88,89. Some support for this idea comes from studies in which teaching children or non-human primates words or symbols for certain concepts (for example, the concept ‘same’) or assigning labels in a way that highlights the task-relevant dimension of the world (for example, drawing attention to object size by labelling a bigger object ‘daddy’ and a smaller one ‘baby’) can lead to success on certain relational reasoning tasks18. Others have argued that training young children on certain syntactic constructions (for example, complement clauses) can result in their ability to pass theory of mind tasks17,90,91. However, reasons for skepticism exist. First, recent evidence suggests that the dissociation between the language network and systems that support thinking and reasoning is already present in young children92,93 (Box 3), which contradicts the possibility that at an early developmental stage thinking relies on linguistic resources. And second, some children growing up with no access to language can nevertheless reason in complex ways. In particular, some deaf children who are born to hearing parents grow up with little or no exposure to language, sometimes for years, because they cannot hear speech and their parents or caregivers do not know sign language. Lack of access to language has harmful consequences for many aspects of cognition94,95, which is to be expected given that language provides a critical source of information for learning about the world96,97. Nevertheless, individuals who experience language deprivation unquestionably exhibit a capacity for complex cognitive function: they can still learn to do mathematics, to engage in relational reasoning, to build causal chains, and to acquire rich and sophisticated knowledge of the world98,99 (also see ref. 100 for more controversial evidence from language deprivation in a case of child abuse). In other words, lack of access to linguistic representations does not make it fundamentally impossible to engage in complex—including symbolic—thought, although some aspects of reasoning do show delays101,102. Thus, it appears that in typical development, language and reasoning develop in parallel (see ‘Communication and thought in humans and animals’ for concordant evidence from brain evolution).

最后值得一提的是，前语言期婴儿103以及许多动物物种——包括非人灵长类104–108、鸦科鸟类109,110、大象111和头足类动物112,113——都表现出令人印象深刻的推理和问题解决能力，而且显然没有语言，这进一步使人质疑语言或类语言系统对于复杂思维的必要性114,115。

Finally, it is worth mentioning that pre-verbal infants103 and many animal species—including non-human primates104–108, corvids109,110, elephants111 and cephalopods112,113—exhibit impressive inferential and problem-solving abilities, apparently without language, further bringing into question the necessity of language or a language-like system for complex thinking114,115.

专栏 3 开放问题

Box 3 Open questions

我们对人类语言能力和认知能力及二者关系的理解仍不完整。这里我们列出几个开放问题。

Our understanding of human linguistic and cognitive capacities and the relationships between them remains incomplete. Here we highlight a few open questions.

(1) 语言选择性脑网络所储存的语言表征的本质是什么？它在理解和产出中执行的计算是什么？人工智能的最新进展——擅长语言的神经网络模型的开发201——为语言研究者提供了一套强大的工具来探究语言加工的神经编码48,202–205（综述见参考文献 206）。这些工具与日益精密的神经记录方法207,208相结合，应能在未来几年推动我们对人类语言系统的理解。

(1) What is the nature of linguistic representations that the language-selective brain network stores and the computations that it performs during comprehension and production? Recent advances in artificial intelligence—the development of neural network models that excel at language201—have provided language researchers with a suite of powerful tools to probe the neural codes of linguistic processing48,202–205 (reviewed in ref. 206). These tools, combined with the increasing sophistication of neural recording approaches207,208, should enable advances in our understanding of the human language system in the coming years.

(2) 我们的思维依赖于符号表征209–212、亚符号或联结主义表征213,214，还是二者的某种组合？介导抽象思维的表征如何从作为我们大脑的生物神经网络中产生215,216？是否有任何与思维相关的计算及其底层神经回路是人类所独有的，还是人类只是拥有更多的神经和认知资源163,173，从而带来更高的复杂程度？

(2) Does our thinking rely on symbolic representations209–212, sub-symbolic or connectionist representations213,214, or some combination of these? How do representations that mediate abstract thought arise from the biological neural networks that are our brains215,216? Are any thought-related computations and the underlying neural circuits distinctly human, or do humans simply have more neural and cognitive resources163,173 that lead to greater sophistication?

(3) 随着儿童学习语言，语言网络是如何发展的？到四岁时已对语言具有选择性的脑区92,93在语言习得之前支持什么认知功能？尽管已有许多研究考察了新生儿和婴儿大脑对言语的反应217–219，但在生命第一年的后半段以及学步期（6 个月至 3 岁）——即儿童开始把词与意义联系起来并以交流方式使用语言的时期——大脑中发生的功能变化仍不清楚，因为在这一年龄段使用 fMRI 等空间精确的脑成像方法进行实验颇具挑战。

(3) How does the language network develop as children learn language? What cognitive functions do brain areas that are selective for language by age four92,93 support before language is acquired? Although a number of studies have investigated responses to speech in newborn and infant brains217–219, the functional changes that happen in the brain during the second half of the first year of life and during toddlerhood (age 6 months to 3 years), when children begin to link words to meanings and to use language communicatively, remain unknown because experimentation with spatially precise brain imaging approaches such as fMRI is challenging at this age.

完好的语言并不意味着完好的思维

Intact language does not imply intact thought

上文讨论的证据表明，迄今测试过的所有类型的思维在没有语言的情况下都是可能的。接下来，我们讨论语言与思维双重分离的另一面：与“语言介导思维”的观点相反，完好的语言系统似乎并不意味着完好的推理能力。来自发育性和获得性脑疾病的证据都表明，即使语言能力基本完好，也可能存在智力损害。例如，若干遗传疾病以不同程度的智力障碍为特征（唐氏综合征和威廉姆斯综合征等），然而这些疾病患者的语言能力似乎接近典型水平。即便观察到细微的语言缺陷，加工词义和构建语言结构的基础能力——即“语言用于思维”假说中所涉及的能力——仍是完好的116–118。某些神经精神疾病（如精神分裂症）会影响思考和推理能力，但同样不累及语言119。最后，许多获得性脑损伤个体在推理和问题解决上存在困难，却似乎完全掌握着自己的语言能力58。换言之，拥有完好的语言系统并不会“免费”附带思维能力：在语言完好的情况下，思维能力也可能受损（来自大语言模型的相关论证见参考文献 120）。

The evidence discussed above suggests that all types of thought tested to date are possible without language. Next, we discuss the other side of the double dissociation between language and thought: contrary to the view that language mediates thinking, an intact language system does not appear to entail intact reasoning abilities. Evidence from both developmental and acquired brain disorders suggests that intellectual impairments can be present even when linguistic abilities are largely intact. For example, several genetic disorders are characterized by varying degrees of intellectual disability (Down syndrome and Williams syndrome, among others), yet the linguistic abilities of people with these disorders appear to be close to typical. Even if subtle linguistic deficits are observed, the foundational capacities for processing word meanings and linguistic structure building—the capacities that figure in the language-for-thought hypotheses—are intact116–118. Some neuropsychiatric disorders, such as schizophrenia, affect the ability to think and reason, but again spare language119. Finally, many individuals with acquired brain damage exhibit difficulties in reasoning and problem solving but appear to have full command of their linguistic abilities58. In other words, having an intact language system does not bring with it ‘for free’ an ability to think: thinking capacities can be impaired in the presence of intact language (see ref. 120 for related arguments from large language models).

语言是一种高效的交流编码

Language is an efficient communication code

在回顾了反对语言在思维中起作用的证据之后，我们接下来讨论交流力量塑造了语言形式的证据2–7。一种高效的交流编码应当易于产出和理解，同时对噪声（环境噪声或因加工机制不完善而产生的噪声）具有鲁棒性21，并且必须能为人所习得。正如我们接下来将讨论的，人类语言——无论是口语还是手语——都表现出所有这些特性，而且这些特性体现在语言结构的各个层面，包括语音、词和句法。

Having reviewed the evidence against the role of language in thought, we next discuss evidence that communicative forces have shaped the form that language takes2–7. An efficient communication code should be easy to produce and understand, while being robust to noise21 (environmental or resulting from imperfect processing mechanisms), and it must be learnable by people. As we discuss next, human languages—both spoken and signed—exhibit all these properties, and these properties manifest at all levels of linguistic structure, including sounds, words and syntax.

我们承认，这些特性中有一些并非“语言用于交流”观点所独有的预测。然而，长期以来，一些“语言用于思维”假说的支持者一直把语言据称缺乏交流特征作为反对语言交流功能的证据121，因此有必要总结现已十分丰富的、表明这些特征在跨语言中稳健存在的证据。此外，某些交流特征在“语言主要用于内部思维”的观点下难以解释。

We acknowledge that some of these properties are not uniquely predicted by the language-for-communication view. However, the supposed absence of communicative features of language has long been used by some advocates of the language-for-thought hypothesis as evidence against the communicative function of language121, so it is important to summarize the now abundant evidence for the robust presence of these features cross-linguistically. Moreover, some of the communicative features are difficult to explain under the view that language is used primarily for internal thought.

从语言结构的最低层级开始，一种语言的语音在语音空间中是分散分布的122,123，这使它们能够以抗噪声干扰的方式承载信息，并促进感知和理解。语言的语音库似乎还受到影响不同音类发音难易的因素塑造，包括物理环境124以及与饮食相关的发音器官解剖结构变化125。

Starting from the lowest level of linguistic structure, the sounds of a language are spread out in phonetic space122,123, which enables them to carry information in a way that is robust to corruption from noise and facilitates perception and comprehension. Sound repertoires of languages appear to also be shaped by factors that affect articulatory ease for different sound classes, including physical environments124 and diet-related changes in the anatomy of the articulatory apparatus125.

就词形而言，语言倾向于重复使用简短高效的词和词内语音序列126。此外，高频词和低信息量的词往往较短127。这些特性使得在产出和理解中提取词语更容易（高频词更容易从记忆中提取），也使发音更省力（短词耗能更少，重复出现的语音序列可以作为组块存储在运动记忆中，从而降低发音计划成本128）。

With respect to word forms, languages preferentially re-use short and efficient words and within-word sound sequences126. Moreover, frequent and low-information words tend to be short127. These properties enable ease of word retrieval in production and comprehension (frequent words are easier to access from memory) and for articulatory ease (short words are less energy-costly, and repeated sound sequences can be stored as chunks in motor memory, reducing articulatory planning costs128).

在词义方面，词语通过在复杂度（习得或表征意义的成本）与信息量（词语选取其意义的精确和无歧义程度）之间进行权衡来优化交流效率。亲属称谓就是一个例子129：不同语言在由“简单意义与信息丰富意义”之间权衡所界定的最优前沿上选择了不同的解决方案（例如，能指出家谱中唯一成员的词，如“外祖母”）。自然语言所具有的这种效率意味着，通常不可能在不减少所传达信息的情况下使一种真实语言的亲属称谓系统大幅简化，反之亦然。颜色词130,131、季节词132以及封闭类词和语法标记133–136也有类似的报告（图 2a）。词汇系统还表现出适应特定交流需求的特征，会更密集地覆盖特定社群所需的概念空间部分137,138。

In terms of word meanings, words optimize communicative efficiency through a trade-off between complexity (the cost of acquiring or representing the meanings) and informativeness (how precisely and unambiguously the words select their meanings). One example is kinship terms129: languages choose different solutions along the optimal frontier defined by the trade-off between having simple versus informative meanings (for example, words that pick out unique members of a family tree, such ‘maternal grandmother’). The efficiency that characterizes natural languages means that it is typically not possible to make a real language’s kinship system much simpler without having it convey less information, or vice versa. Similar results have been reported for colour terms130,131 and season words132, and closed-class words and grammatical markers133–136 (Fig. 2a). Lexical systems also show hallmarks of adaptation to specific communicative needs, more densely covering the parts of a conceptual space that a given community needs137,138.

句法是在“语言是否为高效交流而优化”的讨论中争议最大的语言成分。句法规定了词如何组合以表达海量的意义——即“有限手段的无限运用”139。句法的决定性特性——层级性与组合性——很可能是上文在词义部分提到的同样压力的结果：简洁性压力（对可习得性至关重要）和表达力压力（对有效交流至关重要）5,140–142。此外，世界语言中的各种句法模式也可以通过结合交流压力与认知压力来解释。一个典型例子是语言倾向于最小化词与词之间依存关系的长度。在任何给定的句子中，词语都按照语法规则组合起来，形成更大的意义。例如，在句子“Lana ate five apples”（拉娜吃了五个苹果）中，“five”和“apples”之间存在依存关系，但“Lana”和“five”之间没有联系，因为这两个词在意义上并不直接相关。距离更长的连接（中间隔着更多词的连接）会增加产出和理解的难度，这在行为学测量143,144和脑成像39,45中都得到了证实。很可能正是由于这种认知成本，语言通过最小化依存长度而演化得在加工（即使用）上更为高效145,146（图 2b、c）。语法中保持依存关系局部化的这种功能压力解释了词序中若干普遍倾向147,148。

Syntax is the component of language that has been the most controversial in the discussions about whether languages are optimized for efficient communication. Syntax specifies how words combine to enable the expression of a vast number of meanings—the ‘infinite use of finite means’139. The defining properties of syntax—hierarchy and composition—are probably the result of the very same pressures mentioned in the context of word meanings above: the pressure for simplicity (critical for learnability) and the pressure for expressiveness (critical for effective communication)5,140–142. Moreover, various syntactic patterns in the world’s languages can also be explained by combining communicative and cognitive pressures. A prime example is the tendency of languages to minimize the lengths of dependencies between words. In any given sentence, words are assembled—according to the rules of the grammar—to form a larger meaning. For example, the sentence ‘Lana ate five apples’, has a dependency between ‘five’ and ‘apples’, but there is no link between ‘Lana’ and ‘five’ because those words are not directly related in the meaning. Longer-distance connections (connections with more intervening words) increase difficulty of production and comprehension, as measured behaviourally143,144 or with brain imaging39,45. Plausibly owing to this cognitive cost, languages have evolved to become more efficient for processing—that is, use—by minimizing dependency lengths145,146 (Fig. 2b,c). This functional pressure in a grammar to keep dependencies local explains several universal tendencies in word orders147,148.

其他例子涉及句子中基本成分——主语（大致为施事）、动词和宾语（大致为动作的受事）——的顺序，用以传达复杂意义。主–宾–谓语序是世界语言中最常见的语序（约 47% 的语言，例如日语、波斯语和印地语），它似乎是一种认知上自然的默认语序：说不同语言的人在用手势表达事件意义时都使用这一顺序149，新兴手语也采用这一语序150,151。Gibson 等人152进一步为一些语言从默认的主–宾–谓语序转向第二常见的主–谓–宾语序（约 41% 的语言，例如英语、乌克兰语和汉语普通话）提供了交流方面的解释。具体而言，在主–谓–宾语序中，当交流中出现信息丢失时，听者可以利用位置线索——某个名词出现在动词之前还是之后——来重建“谁对谁做了什么”153,154（参考文献 155–157 描述了源于类似压力的其他词序概括）。

Other examples concern the order of basic elements—the subject (the agent, roughly), verb and object (the patient of the action, roughly)—within a sentence to convey complex meanings. The subject–object–verb order, which is the most common across the world’s languages (approximately 47% of languages—for example, Japanese, Persian and Hindi), appears to be a cognitively natural default: speakers of diverse languages use this order when gesturing event meanings149, and emergent sign languages have this order150,151. Gibson et al.152 have further offered a communicative explanation for the shift of some languages from the default (subject–object–verb) order to the second most common order, subject–verb–object (approximately 41% of languages—for example, English, Ukrainian and Mandarin). In particular, in the subject–verb–object order, the listener can use positional cues—whether a given noun appears before or after the verb—to reconstruct who is doing what to whom in the presence of information loss during communication153,154 (refs. 155–157 describe other word-order generalizations that follow from similar pressures).

反对“语言是作为交流系统而演化”这一观点的一个常见论据是歧义的普遍存在：大多数词有多种意义，许多句子（尤其是较长的句子）有多种可能的依存结构。例如，Chomsky 长期以来认为，歧义的存在意味着语言主要用于思维而非交流，因为有歧义的信号会妨碍交流121。然而，在“语言用于思维”的观点下，人类语言中存在歧义实际上并不在预期之中，因为我们的思想似乎并不含糊。相反，歧义的存在是语言交流理论的自然预测。也就是说，可以从数学上证明歧义在交流上是有用的：它不仅允许说话者省略听者已知的信息（例如从语境中已知的信息），还使简短、易于产出的语言形式得以重复使用158。一个不允许任何歧义的系统将需要比人类语言系统大得多的词库和语法，而且即便要传达简单的意义，也需要使用很长的词和句子。例如，一种为消除歧义而构建的人造语言159被证明过于复杂，以至于人类无法习得，并且已经历多轮修订以提高可学性。此外，有观点认为，具有多个相关义项的词（例如“water”既可作名词表示饮用的水，也可作动词表示浇水）有助于学习，因为习得一个意义会有助于习得相关的另一个意义160。由此看来，支持多重形式–意义映射的能力很可能有助于维持丰富的词库。

One common argument against the idea that language has evolved as a communication system is the prevalence of ambiguity: most words have multiple meanings, and many (especially longer) sentences have many possible dependency structures. Chomsky, for instance, has long argued that the existence of ambiguity implies that language is used primarily for thought rather than communication, because ambiguous signals would impede communication121. However, the existence of ambiguity in human language is actually not expected under the language-for-thought view, given that our thoughts do not seem ambiguous. By contrast, the existence of ambiguity in language is a natural prediction of communicative accounts of language. That is, ambiguity can be mathematically shown to be communicatively useful: not only does it allow speakers to leave out information that listeners already know (for example, from the context), but it enables the re-use of short, easy-to-produce linguistic forms158. A system that allows no ambiguity would require a much bigger lexicon and grammar than those of human linguistic systems, and such a system would need to use long words and sentences to convey even simple meanings. For example, an artificial language that was constructed to remove ambiguity159 proved to be so complicated as to be unlearnable by humans and has been undergoing rounds of revision to allow for learnability. Moreover, the existence of words with multiple related senses (such as ‘water’ used as a drink and as a verb) has been argued to support learning, since acquisition of one meaning will help with acquisition of a related one160. In this way, the capacity for multiple form–meaning mappings is likely to be useful for maintaining a rich lexicon.

我们承认，人类语言的某些特性也可能有非交流性的解释。例如，语言的组合性可能只是反映了思维中、甚至较低层级的感知和运动系统中预先存在的组合性161——不过这一观点仍与“语言用于思维”假说相悖，因为其方向是反过来的。

We acknowledge that some of these properties of human languages may also have non-communicative explanations. For example, compositionality in language may simply reflect pre-existing compositionality in thought, or even in lower-level, perceptual and motor systems161—although this idea is still contrary to the language-for-thought hypothesis, as the directionality is reversed.

人类与动物中的交流与思维

Communication and thought in humans and animals

在各个物种中，与同类的互动都需要一个交流系统——即感知和发出信号的机制，以及信号–意义关联的储存。人类的交流系统无疑是复杂的，但语言是否赋予了我们一种新的推理形式（专栏 1），还是语言只是反映了人类思想独立存在的复杂精妙？在这篇观点文章中，我们在前人理论的基础上，结合过去二十年的证据，论证了语言似乎并不是迄今测试过的任何形式思维所必需的，而且语言对思维也不是充分的。此外，基于自然语言的许多特征似乎都为高效信息传递而优化这一证据，我们论证了交流是语言的首要功能。

Across species, interactions with conspecifics require a communication system—that is, mechanisms for perceiving and emitting signals and a store of signal-to-meaning associations. The communication system of humans is unquestionably complex, but did language endow us with a new form of reasoning (Box 1), or does language simply reflect the independent sophistication of human thoughts? In this Perspective, building on prior theorizing and bringing in evidence from the past two decades, we have argued that language appears to not be necessary for any forms of thought tested so far, and that language is not sufficient for thought. Furthermore, on the basis of the evidence that many features of natural languages appear to be optimized for efficient information transfer, we have argued for communication being the primary function of language.

“语言只是一个交流系统”的观点与人类进化的连续性观点相一致162,163。按照这一观点，人类语言的特性——包括其复杂性——可能源于语言演化所处的多方面环境：在这一环境中，该系统必须有用（能够表达人类心智的内部内容）且可习得，而人类应能够以既有认知和神经系统所特有的优势与局限来加工语言。与之相对的另一种观点——语言是思维的基质——则意味着我们这一物种与其他物种之间存在截然的不连续性。这种观点把语言（或许是先天的）置于中心，视其为变化的机制，以及赋予人类一种用于心理计算的新型表征格式的机制。

The view that language is simply a communication system aligns with a continuity view of human evolution162,163. In this view, the properties of human language—including its complexity—may result from the multifaceted landscape in which it has evolved, where the system must be useful (able to express the internal contents of the human mind) and learnable, and humans should be able to process language with the idiosyncratic strengths and limitations of pre-existing cognitive and neural systems. The contrasting alternative—that language is the substrate for thinking—implies a sharp discontinuity between our species and others. This alternative view centres language—perhaps innately—as the mechanism of change, and the mechanism that endowed humans with a novel representational format for mental computations.

为什么语言与思维之间的密切关系对许多人具有直觉上的吸引力？有些人执着于“人类在动物界中具有优越性”的观念（即人类与其他动物存在质的差异而不仅是量的差异164），尽管科学证据表明人类与非人动物之间存在很强的生物学相似性165,166。另一个原因可能与在解释人类与非人动物差异时追求简约有关（其他原因见补充信息）。具体而言，人类在交流系统以及思想和认知的复杂精妙程度上都不同于其他动物。简约的解释倾向于单一因素的说明——例如，人类进化出了语言，而认知的变化只是其结果。然而，来自人脑进化的证据反而表明，多个认知系统的复杂程度是平行提高的。

Why does an intimate relationship between language and thought have an intuitive appeal to many? Some are attached to the idea that humans are superior in the animal kingdom (that is, they differ qualitatively, not just quantitatively, from other animals164), even though scientific evidence suggests strong biological similarities between humans and non-human animals165,166. Another reason may be linked to the desire for parsimony in explaining differences between humans and non-human animals (additional reasons are provided in Supplementary Information). In particular, humans differ from other animals in the sophistication of their communication system as well as their thoughts and cognition. A parsimonious account favours a single-factor explanation—for instance, humans evolved language, and the change in cognition was simply a consequence of this. However, evidence from human brain evolution instead suggests parallel increases in the sophistication of multiple cognitive systems.

与其他动物（包括非人灵长类）的大脑相比，联合皮层——承载着超越感知和运动控制的心理过程——在人脑中显著且不成比例地扩张了167。联合皮层跨越额叶、颞叶和顶叶，在人类中由多个大规模网络组成——即共同支持认知某一方面的脑区集合75。语言网络28只是这些网络之一。在刻画支持人类认知能力的若干其他网络方面已取得重大进展，包括那些支持“语言对于思维既不必要也不充分”一节中所讨论的非语言任务的网络。例如，有时被称为“多重需求”网络的网络支持多种目标导向行为，包括新颖问题的解决，该网络受损会导致流体智力受损168（图 1b）。数学和逻辑推理以及计算机代码的加工也依赖多重需求网络78–83。其他此类网络包括支持社会推理（包括心理化，即思考他人的想法）的“心理理论”网络169（图 1b），以及“默认”网络——其功能仍有争论，有人将其区域与向过去或未来的情景投射联系起来170，另一些人则将其与空间认知和推理联系起来171。至少其中某些网络在非人动物大脑中有同源结构172——跨物种功能架构的对应关系是神经科学中一项正在进行的工作。

Relative to the brains of other animals, including non-human primates, the association cortex—which houses mental processes above and beyond perception and motor control—has expanded substantially and disproportionately in the human brain167. The association cortex spans frontal, temporal and parietal lobes and, in humans, comprises multiple large-scale networks—ensembles of brain areas that jointly support some aspect of cognition75. The language network28 is just one of these networks. Significant progress has been made in characterizing several other networks that support human cognitive abilities, including those underlying the non-linguistic tasks discussed in ‘Language is not necessary or sufficient for thought’. For example, the network sometimes referred to as the ‘multiple demand’ network, supports diverse goal-directed behaviours, including novel problem solving, and damage of this network leads to impairments in fluid intelligence168 (Fig. 1b). Mathematical and logical reasoning and the processing of computer code also draw on the multiple demand network78–83. Other such networks include the ‘theory of mind’ network, which supports social reasoning, including mentalizing or thinking about others’ thoughts169 (Fig. 1b) and the ‘default’ network, whose functions remain debated, with some linking its regions to episodic projection into the past or future170 and others linking them to spatial cognition and reasoning171. At least some of the networks have homologues in non-human animal brains172—the correspondences in functional architecture across species is an ongoing effort in neuroscience.

然而重要的是，在人类进化过程中有多个脑网络发生了扩张，而这种扩张与多种认知能力的提升相关联173。这种扩张究竟是真正平行进行的，还是某一个网络的出现或扩张关键地驱动了其他网络的扩张，目前尚不清楚；但前一种可能性或许更合理，因为多种认知能力很可能都提高了生存概率——包括社会复杂性（能够对他人心智建模）、推断世界中因果结构的能力、灵活的问题解决和为未来做计划的能力，以及更好的交流能力。无论现代人类大脑中不同认知网络扩张的确切时间线和顺序如何，语言网络——支持我们与同类交流的能力——与支持我们思考和推理能力的网络截然不同，这使得“语言介导思维”的观点不太可能成立。

Importantly, however, multiple brain networks have expanded over the course of human evolution, and this expansion was associated with increases in diverse cognitive abilities173. Whether this expansion proceeded in a truly parallel fashion, or whether the emergence or expansion of one network critically drove the expansion of other networks is not known, but the former possibility is perhaps more plausible given that diverse cognitive abilities probably increased the probability of survival—including social sophistication (being able to model the minds of others), the ability to infer causal structures in the world, flexible problem solving and planning for the future, and better communicative ability. Regardless of the exact timeline and order of the expansion of different cognitive networks in the brains of modern humans, the language network—which supports our ability to communicate with conspecifics—is sharply distinct from the networks that support our abilities to think and reason, which makes the idea that language mediates thinking unlikely.

结论

Conclusions

总之，我们回顾了过去二十年的研究工作，这些工作有助于阐明语言在现代人类中的功能及其在人类认知中的作用。来自失语症研究的证据表明，所有已测试形式的思维在没有语言的情况下都是可能的；fMRI 证据表明，从事多种形式的思维和推理并不会调用语言网络——即在语言理解和产出过程中表征和加工词义与句法结构的一组脑区。此外，完好的语言能力并不意味着完好的思维能力。综合来看，这些证据表明语言不太可能是任何形式思维的关键基质。尽管接触词语、句法结构或非语言符号可以促进某些认知任务的表现（专栏 1），但语言与思维和推理是双重分离的（关于语言表征和介导思维的心理表征之本质的开放问题，参见专栏 3）。

In sum, we have reviewed work from the past two decades that has helped to clarify the function of language in modern humans and its role in human cognition. Evidence from aphasia research suggests that all tested forms of thought are possible in the absence of language, and fMRI evidence suggests that engaging in diverse forms of thinking and reasoning does not recruit the language network—a set of brain areas that represent and process word meanings and syntactic structure during language comprehension and production. Moreover, intact linguistic abilities do not entail intact thinking abilities. Together, this evidence suggests that language is unlikely to be a critical substrate for any form of thought. Although access to words, syntactic structures or non-linguistic symbols can facilitate performance on certain cognitive tasks (Box 1), language is doubly dissociated from thinking and reasoning (compare with Box 3 for open questions about the nature of linguistic and thought-mediating mental representations).

我们还回顾了一系列研究，它们表明人类语言的多种特性使其易于产出、易于学习和理解、简洁高效且对噪声具有鲁棒性。其中许多跨语言倾向——包括最小化依存长度的倾向、对特定词序的偏好以及歧义的普遍存在——在“语言用于内部思维”的观点下、且不诉诸语言如何被使用和加工的情况下，是难以解释的。

We have also reviewed a body of work that has shown that diverse properties of human languages render them easy to produce, easy to learn and understand, concise and efficient for use, and robust to noise. Many of these cross-linguistic tendencies—including the tendency to minimize dependency lengths, the preferences for particular word orders, and the prevalence of ambiguity—are difficult to account for under the view that language is used for internal thought and without appealing to how language is used and processed.

综合考虑这些证据，我们认为语言主要服务于交流功能，它反映了而非造就了人类认知标志性的复杂精妙。语言很可能并不是为思维和推理提供关键基质，而是通过实现所获知识的跨代传递改变了我们这一物种。语言无疑是传递知识的极其有用的工具。这种传递的累积效应——知识建立在知识之上——连同我们社会能力和问题解决能力复杂性的提高，很可能正是使我们得以创造人类文明的原因174–177。尽管我们的回顾表明，所有已测试形式的思维在没有语言的情况下显然都是可能的，但如果没有语言的外部使用所促成的累积文化，我们这一物种的成功恐怕是不可能的。

Considering the evidence in tandem, we have argued that language serves a primarily communicative function and reflects, rather than gives rise to, the signature sophistication of human cognition. Instead of providing the key substrate for thinking and reasoning, language likely transformed our species by enabling cross-generational transmission of acquired knowledge. Language is uncontroversially a tremendously useful tool for knowledge transmission. The cumulative effect of this transmission—knowledge building on knowledge—along with increased sophistication of our social and problem-solving abilities is plausibly what enabled us to create human civilizations174–177. Although our review shows that all tested forms of thought are apparently possible without language, it is unlikely that our species’ success would have been possible without the cumulative culture that was enabled by the external usage of language.
